title: Orbit-separated two-section pencils from an ample power
statement: Let $F$ be any field [def-weil-field], including a finite field. Let $Y$ be a nonempty projective finite-type $F$-scheme of topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-projective, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $L$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Let $G$ be a finite group acting on $Y$ by $F$-automorphisms; faithfulness is not required. Using module pullback and sheaf tensor product [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], put $B=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*L$. For $d\geq1$ and $a\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes d})$, put $\mathcal N_G(a)=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*a\in\Gamma(Y,B^{\otimes d})$, using the canonical permutation of tensor factors. There exist $d\geq1$ and $a,b\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes d})$ such that the two closed subsets $\bigcup_{g\in G}g^{-1}Z(a)$ and $\bigcup_{g\in G}g^{-1}Z(b)$ are disjoint; here $Z(a)$ is the locus where the residue-field value of $a$ is zero. The sections $a,b$ generate $L^{\otimes d}$, and $\mathcal N_G(a),\mathcal N_G(b)$ generate $B^{\otimes d}$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. Both morphisms $[a:b]$ and $[\mathcal N_G(a):\mathcal N_G(b)]:Y\to\mathbf P^1_F$ given by those sections are finite [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; the latter is $G$-invariant. No smoothness, reducedness, irreducibility, or infinitude of $F$ is assumed.

proof.text: The field $F$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$; $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is a one-point Noetherian affine scheme. Thus $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [lem-sfb-ample-orbit-affine-pair] to obtain $p,q>0$, sections $u,v$, affine opens $U=Y_u,V=Y_v$, and the finite $G$-stable set $T=\bigcup_g g^{-1}Z(u)\subseteq V$.

source.place: Tag 09NV (lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine); morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); preparation packaged in the first new node.

proof.text: Set $d=pq>0$, $a=u^{\otimes q}$ and $b=v^{\otimes p}$. The tensor identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] put both in $L^{\otimes d}$. In a one-dimensional residue fibre, a positive tensor power vanishes exactly when its scalar coefficient vanishes. Hence $Y_a=U$, $Y_b=V$, and $\bigcup_g g^{-1}Z(a)=T$. If $y\in T$ then $hy\in T\subseteq V$ for every $h$, so $b(hy)\ne0$. Thus the two orbit zero unions are disjoint, and the identity element gives $Z(a)\cap Z(b)=\varnothing$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre], $a,b$ generate $L^{\otimes d}$.

$Y$ is proper over $F$ by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. The tensor closure in [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] makes $M=L^{\otimes d}$ invertible. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-orbit-pair-finite-norm] to $M$ and the affine, orbit-separated pair from step 2. Put $C=\bigotimes_g g^*M$. The criterion gives invertibility of $C$, generation by its norm pair, and finite ordinary and invariant norm coordinate maps. The section-compatible pullback-tensor isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], followed by associating and permuting the finitely many tensor factors, give $\beta:C\cong B^{\otimes d}$. They send $\bigotimes_g g^*a$ to $\mathcal N_G(a)$ and $\bigotimes_g g^*b$ to $\mathcal N_G(b)$ under the definition of those sections. Thus $B^{\otimes d}$ is invertible and its norm pair generates. Equivalence of generating pairs in [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] identifies the two norm coordinate morphisms over $\mathbf Z$; together with their identical structure map to $\operatorname{Spec}F$, this identifies them over $F$. Finiteness and scheme-level $G$-invariance therefore hold for the stated norm map; the ordinary map is the supplied $[a:b]$.
